exercises.title: Target sum: + or − before every number — turn it into counting subsets
concepts: P − N = target, P + N = sum ⇒ P = (sum + target)/2
exercises.problemHtml:
a holds non-negative ints. Put + or − in front of every number; complete static long ways(int[] a, int target): in how many ways the result equals target, modulo 1,000,000,007. Example {2,1,3,1,1}, target 2 → 5; {0,0,1}, target 1 → 4 (+0 and −0 are different choices).

If P = sum of the "+" numbers and N of the "−" ones, P − N = target and P + N = sum, so P = (sum + target)/2: count subsets with sum P (0 if |target| > sum or sum + target is odd). cnt[s] += cnt[s − x] with s going down so that each number is used once. The complexity check has 200 numbers — 2²⁰⁰ sign patterns.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 200 numbers, sum ≤ 10,000) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n · sum) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(2ⁿ) (trying every sign) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

node cham.mjs

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Windows (PowerShell): cd "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\<folder>" — cmd: cd /d %USERPROFILE%\Downloads\<folder> — then node cham.mjs. macOS (Terminal): cd ~/Downloads/<folder> then node cham.mjs. Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

Requirements
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
a gồm các số nguyên không âm. Đặt + hoặc − trước mỗi số; hoàn thiện ways(a, target): có bao nhiêu cách để kết quả bằng target, lấy dư 1.000.000.007. Ví dụ {2,1,3,1,1}, target 2 → 5; {0,0,1}, target 1 → 4 (+0 và −0 là hai lựa chọn khác nhau).

Gọi P = tổng các số mang "+", N = tổng các số mang "−": P − N = target và P + N = sum, nên P = (sum + target)/2: đếm tập con có tổng P (0 nếu |target| > sum hoặc sum + target lẻ). cnt[s] += cnt[s − x] với s đi xuống để mỗi số dùng một lần. Kiểm độ phức tạp có 200 số — 2²⁰⁰ cách đặt dấu.

⏱ Kiểm độ phức tạp. Một ca chạy code của bạn với input LỚN (n = 200 numbers, sum ≤ 10,000) trong hạn 3 giây. Lời giải O(n · sum) xong trong chưa tới một giây trên laptop bình thường; bản O(2ⁿ) (trying every sign) cần lâu hơn rất nhiều và ca in TOO SLOW. Hạn đặt rộng có chủ ý — trượt ca này thì do thuật toán, không phải do máy bạn.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: The algebra turns 2ⁿ sign patterns into "how many subsets have sum P" — a 0/1 counting knapsack over sums 0…P: O(n · sum) time, O(sum) memory.

exercises.title: Longest common subarray (contiguous!) — not the LCS
concepts: dp[i][j] = common block ENDING at a[i−1], b[j−1]
exercises.problemHtml:
Complete static int longest(int[] a, int[] b): the length of the longest contiguous block that appears in both arrays. Example {5,1,2,8,3,7} and {1,2,3,7,8} → 2 ([1,2] or [3,7]); the LCS (which may skip) would be 4.

dp[i][j] = length of the common block that ends exactly at a[i−1] and b[j−1]: equal → dp[i−1][j−1] + 1, different → 0. The answer is the maximum cell, not dp[n][m]. The complexity check uses two arrays of 3000 that share long blocks.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 3000 × 3000) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n · m) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an O(n · m · L) (extending from every pair of starts) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

The zip unpacks into a folder named after the exercise (<folder> below). Tip: type cd and drag the folder into the terminal window. You need Node.js 18+ and JDK 8 or newer (17 or 21 recommended) — javac -version must work.

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Hoàn thiện longest(a, b): độ dài khối liên tiếp dài nhất xuất hiện trong cả hai mảng. Ví dụ {5,1,2,8,3,7} và {1,2,3,7,8} → 2 ([1,2] hoặc [3,7]); LCS (được bỏ qua phần tử) sẽ là 4.

dp[i][j] = độ dài khối chung kết thúc đúng tại a[i−1] và b[j−1]: bằng nhau → dp[i−1][j−1] + 1, khác → 0. Đáp án là ô lớn nhất, không phải dp[n][m]. Kiểm độ phức tạp dùng hai mảng 3000 phần tử có chung những khối dài.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: "Ending exactly here" is the key state for contiguous problems: it makes a mismatch a reset to 0 and the global answer a maximum over all states. n·m cells, O(1) each.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: "Kết thúc đúng ở đây" là trạng thái then chốt của các bài liên tiếp: nó biến chỗ khác nhau thành đặt lại về 0 và đáp án chung thành max trên mọi trạng thái. n·m ô, mỗi ô O(1).

mistakesJson.loi: Copying the LCS recurrence max(dp[i−1][j], dp[i][j−1]) — that allows gaps.|||Chép công thức LCS max(dp[i−1][j], dp[i][j−1]) — công thức đó cho phép có khoảng trống.

exercises.title: Is c an interleaving of a and b? — a 2-D boolean table (greedy fails)
concepts: dp[i][j]: a[0..i) and b[0..j) form c[0..i+j)
last character from a or from b
exercises.problemHtml:
Complete static boolean can(String a, String b, String c): can c be obtained by merging a and b while keeping the order of characters inside each? Examples: a = abc, b = xab: c = axbabc → true, abcxba → false. a = ab, b = ac, c = acab → true, although taking from a whenever it matches fails.

dp[i][j] = the first i characters of a and the first j of b can form the first i + j of c: true if (dp[i−1][j] and a[i−1] = c[i+j−1]) or (dp[i][j−1] and b[j−1] = c[i+j−1]). Check the lengths first. The complexity check uses strings of 2000 a’s.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 2000 + 2000 characters) inside a 3-second limit. An O(n · m) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an exponential (plain recursion on repeated letters) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

Run the grader on your machine

The website does NOT grade this exercise. Press Tải .zip (download) above the code, unzip it, edit the code in src/, then inside the exercise folder (the one with cham.mjs) run:

The grader compiles src/ with javac, runs 3 case(s) (2 hidden — not printed in this text), compares your output line by line (trailing spaces and Windows/macOS line endings ignored), prints a diff of the wrong lines and gives a score. When it prints ALL CHECKS PASSED, come back and press Tự đánh dấu đã giải (self-mark as solved). node cham.mjs --case 2 --show prints the input and your whole output for case 2.

exercises.title: In how many ways can t be picked out of s? — distinct subsequences
concepts: j goes DOWN (each s[i] used once)
exercises.problemHtml:
Complete static long count(String s, String t): the number of ways to choose positions of s (in order) that spell t, modulo 1,000,000,007. Examples: s = banana: t = ban → 3, t = ana → 4, t = "" → 1. 60 a’s choosing 30 gives C(60, 30) — beyond an int.

dp[j] = number of ways to form t[0..j) from the part of s read so far, dp[0] = 1. For each character of s, for j from |t| down to 1: if s[i] = t[j−1], dp[j] += dp[j−1]. O(|s|·|t|); the complexity check has |s| = 20,000, |t| = 300.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = |s| = 20,000, |t| = 300) inside a 3-second limit. An O(|s| · |t|) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an exponential (every choice of positions) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

exercises.title: Dungeon: the smallest starting health — fill the table BACKWARDS
concepts: need[r][c] = health needed when ENTERING (r, c)
exercises.problemHtml:
A knight walks from the top-left to the bottom-right cell of g moving only right or down; g[r][c] is added to his health (negative = damage). Health must stay ≥ 1 at every moment, including after the last cell. Complete static int start(int[][] g): the smallest starting health. Example [-2,-4,3] [-6,8,-1] [9,-12,5] → 7.

Going forward you would need two numbers per cell (health left and lowest point so far) and neither alone decides. Going backwards one number suffices: need[r][c] = max(1, min(need[r+1][c], need[r][c+1]) − g[r][c]), with 1 needed after the exit. The complexity check is a 1000 × 1000 grid.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = 1000 × 1000 grid) inside a 3-second limit. An O(R · C) solution finishes in a fraction of a second on any ordinary laptop; an exponential (every path) one needs far longer and the case prints TOO SLOW. The limit is generous on purpose — if it fails, the algorithm is the problem, not your machine.

exercises.title: Fewest cuts so that every piece is a palindrome — two DP tables
exercises.problemHtml:
Complete static int minCuts(String s): the fewest cuts that split s into palindromes (0 for an empty string or a palindrome). Examples: abaccd → 2 (aba|cc|d), aab → 1, racecar → 0, abcd → 3. Greedy "cut off the longest palindromic prefix" gives 2 for abaab, the answer is 1 (a|baab).

Step 1: pal[i][j] = s[i] == s[j] && (j − i < 2 || pal[i+1][j−1]), filled with i going down. Step 2: cut[j] = fewest cuts for s[0..j]: the last piece is some palindrome s[i..j], so cut[j] = min(i == 0 ? 0 : cut[i−1] + 1). O(n²); the complexity check has n = 2000.

⏱ Complexity check. One case runs your code on a large input (n = n = 2000) inside a 3-second limit. Java 8+ syntax only (it must also compile on the JDK 8 of the exam room); no build tool — plain javac. Main class: KiemTra.|||Cú pháp Java 8 (phải biên dịch được cả trên JDK 8 của phòng thi); không cần công cụ build — javac thuần. Lớp chạy: KiemTra.

hintsJson: pal[i][j] needs pal[i+1][j−1], a row BELOW — so fill i from n − 1 down to 0.|||pal[i][j] cần pal[i+1][j−1], ở hàng DƯỚI — nên điền i từ n − 1 xuống 0.
If s[0..j] is itself a palindrome, cut[j] = 0 — that is the i == 0 case.|||Nếu chính s[0..j] là palindrome thì cut[j] = 0 — đó là trường hợp i == 0.

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: Two O(n²) tables: an interval DP that answers "is s[i..j] a palindrome" in O(1), and a prefix DP over the last piece. Precomputing the first table is what keeps the second one quadratic instead of cubic.
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Hai bảng O(n²): một bảng quy hoạch theo đoạn trả lời "s[i..j] có là palindrome" trong O(1), và một bảng theo tiền tố trên mảnh cuối. Tính trước bảng thứ nhất là điều giữ bảng thứ hai ở mức bình phương thay vì lập phương.

mistakesJson.loi: Testing palindromes with substring + reverse inside the double loop — O(n³), too slow for 2000.|||Kiểm palindrome bằng substring + reverse trong vòng lặp đôi — O(n³), quá chậm với 2000.
Greedy longest prefix — abaab gives aba|a|b (2 cuts) instead of a|baab.|||Tham lam tiền tố dài nhất — abaab ra aba|a|b (2 lần cắt) thay vì a|baab.
